title: IT Fresher Hiring Rebounds After Five-Year Slide as Agrani Lines Up Rs 800 Crore Raise
excerpt: TCS, Infosys and HCLTech hired about 19,000 entry-level staff in the June quarter as annual intake climbs back from its FY26 low — while semiconductor startup Agrani Labs negotiates a Rs 800-850 crore round led by Peak XV, Samsung and 360 One.
body:
• Entry-level hiring by India's top IT firms is rebounding after a five-year slide — TCS, Infosys and HCLTech recruited about 19,000 freshers in the June quarter, per Nasscom data covering 29 IT services firms.
  • Annual fresher intake fell from 380,000 in FY22 to roughly 110,000 in FY26; campus intake improved 25% in H1 FY26 versus a year earlier, Adecco reports.
  • The bar for freshers has risen sharply: firms now want AI, cloud, data and cybersecurity skills ready from day one, not capabilities built on the job.
  • Bengaluru semiconductor startup Agrani Labs is in talks to raise Rs 800-850 crore from Samsung, 360 One and Peak XV at a post-money valuation of Rs 2,400-2,500 crore.

India's IT job engine is finally turning again. After five years of shrinking entry-level intake — from 380,000 in FY22 to roughly 110,000 in FY26 — the country's top IT services firms have resumed campus hiring at pace. TCS, Infosys and HCLTech together recruited about 19,000 entry-level staff in the June quarter, according to Nasscom's September quarter report covering 29 IT services firms.

The recovery is broad. For the first time in two years, India's top four IT companies — TCS, Cognizant, Infosys and Wipro — all reported positive net employee hiring in the September quarter, driven by a return to campus recruitment and fresh project signings. TCS added a net 5,726 associates in the quarter, taking its workforce to 612,724, and says it remains on track for fresher onboarding this year with recruitment for FY27 already underway through the National Qualifier Test.

Context & Background

The slide was long and steady: FY23 intake fell to 250,000, FY24 to 155,000 and FY25 to 125,000. The Economic Times reported that the June-quarter rebound marks the first real break in the decline. Utilisation rates above 85% left firms with little slack, forcing them to hire to meet project demand.

But this is not the old hiring playbook returning. Campus intake improved 25% in H1 FY26 compared to a year earlier, with demand for engineering, technical and AI profiles up 27% and compensation 5% higher, Adecco Group reported. Companies have shifted from "hire-and-train" to "train-then-hire," engaging campuses earlier so freshers arrive project-ready. TeamLease EdTech's July-December 2026 outlook puts overall fresher hiring intent at 75% — though IT itself dipped to 76% from 81%, as employers in tech and consulting get more selective about skills.

"Our workforce at the end of the second quarter was 612,724. We added a net 5,726 associates this quarter... We remain on track for freshers on boarding as planned for the year."

— Milind Lakkad, Chief HR Officer, TCS

Colleges report earlier and stronger placements. Rajalakshmi Engineering College says nearly 50% of its placements happened in June and July itself, and about 65% of TCS roles were at its Digital and Prime levels, paying ₹7-12 lakh per annum.

Impact & Analysis

The message to the 2027 graduating class is blunt: fewer seats, higher bar. Experts told The Economic Times that firms increasingly demand specialised capabilities in AI, cloud, data and cybersecurity to keep ramp-up time minimal. As TeamLease EdTech CEO Shantanu Rooj put it, IT employers now expect freshers to show AI fluency and hands-on project experience "from day one, not capabilities they'll build on the job."

Parallel to the hiring rebound, capital is flowing into India's semiconductor ambitions. Bengaluru-based Agrani Labs is in talks to raise Rs 800-850 crore — including from Samsung, 360 One Asset Management and existing backer Peak XV Partners — at a post-money valuation of about Rs 2,400-2,500 crore, according to people familiar with the matter cited by ET. Peak XV is likely to put in Rs 180-200 crore, and the company may tap Rs 120-130 crore under the government's RDI scheme.

Diaspora Angle

For the vast Indian tech diaspora, the hiring rebound signals a healthier pipeline of India-based talent feeding global delivery centres — and the Agrani raise underscores how semiconductor bets in Bengaluru are drawing capital from Korean and global investors, not just domestic funds.

What's Next

Watch the December quarter: campus drives from TCS, Cognizant and Accenture are rolling out now, and the test will be whether hiring momentum survives past the initial rebound or stalls as firms hit their FY27 intake targets.
